newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Europe hits maximum gas oil output as price soars.
newsitem.headline: Europe hits maximum gas oil output as price soars.

text.p: European refiners reached maximum gas oil output in September as prices soared, but they will need to stay at that peak to replenish low stocks, traders and analysts say.
"All the evidence so far is that they've not been able to keep up," said Geoff Pyne, energy economist at UBS in London.

Production of middle distillates in September reached 5.273 million barrels per day (bpd), a modest 4,000 bpd (0.1 percent) on August, but 139,000 bpd (2.7 percent) higher than in September 1995, Euroilstock said in its monthly report of the 14 countries of the European Union, excluding Sweden.

The increased middle distillate yield came at the expense of gasoline output, which declined by 20,000 bpd in September to 3.195 million bpd, 111,000 bpd (3.4 percent) lower than at the same time last year.
Some analysts expressed surprise that majors had managed to squeeze extra gas oil from their refineries.
"I can see they would want to increase (the gas oil output), but I'm a little surprised that they have managed to do so by so much," said Cindy Poynter of oil consultants Bonner and Moore.

However, even though late summer marks the start of the gas oil production season, the incentive to produce has been huge this year. Benchmark IPE gas oil futures rose 40 percent in the third quarter this year and the crack against Brent crude has, on some occasions, reached $8 a barrel. Gasoline prices, by contrast, were only 10 percent higher than at the start of the third quarter.
"There's a quite fantastic incentive (to maximise gas oil output)," said Pyne.

Enhanced revenue from low sulphur diesel has also increased the allure of gas oil for refiners. Analysts estimate the extra cost of producing 0.05 percent sulphur diesel is about $4 a tonne, ignoring capital investments. The premium of diesel over 0.2 percent sulphur heating oil has, however, reached about $30 a tonne.

However, despite all the efforts to maximise gas oil, Europe remains in shortfall as evidenced by Euroil stock report earlier this month. The report showed middle distillate stocks fell 2.93 million barrels, or 1.0 percent, in September to 283.35 million barrels, a year-on-year deficit of 33.47 million barrels, or 10.6 percent.
"A lot of people will be looking very closely at October's stock levels," said Pyne.
